keyFindings.description: An 'inert' card (steer, triggerTurn false, 1048-1050) handed while a turn streams goes into omp's steering queue, and omp runs another model turn on a steering message at the stop boundary; triggerTurn is ignored while streaming. Deep-review drove it on real omp 18.12.2 with claude-haiku-4-5: the model answered the replayed BTW ('17 x 23 = 391') in the main transcript. The tester's legs ran on an idle host (B5, B6k) or interrupted before the stop boundary (B7). So a replayed BTW, or a failure notice naming one, still starts a turn when it arrives mid-turn. Hold an inert card until the host is idle with no pending messages (the heartbeat's isIdle/hasPendingMessages gate) and hand it then; correct unwritten-frames.ts 6-11, pi-envoy AGENTS.md, the CHANGELOG and the PR body.

readArrivals checks `stopped` (200-201) before shifting `arrived`, so frames already read from a subscription that then ends cleanly (unsubscribe, channel close, connection close) while an earlier delivery is slow are dropped. nats.js QueuedIteratorImpl yields the batch it took before it honours done; code-quality proved it on nats 2.29.3's own iterator (raw [1,2,3], through readArrivals [1]). Role-held topics and anything replay does not cover are lost silently. Yield what was read before ending; the test's hand-made fake pins the wrong model, so drive it with nats.js's iterator.

The trust sentence (178-181) says 'a live session's id'; replayHandler never checks liveness, so any session id whose inbox the stream still holds, an ended session's included, is readable, and 'reach the listener' means holding its API credential, or loopback when /v1 is open. Same in the census rollout line.

The pump comment (1536-1537) says the next sweep shows a failed frame or deliver reported it; a BTW is recorded before its side turn, so when both its reply POSTs fail no sweep shows it and no notice comes. Dispatch records the attempt unanswered and a Retry runs, so that is not a defect; correct the comment.

Hypothesis (not driven): cursorStarts is stamped when the answer arrives, after the listener read its watermark, so a frame stored before the watermark but delivered on the NATS socket after the HTTP answer is stamped after the cursor start and is only logged if it fails. A short grace margin on the start biases it to a notice.
